issues.problem: The rule Silver Bullet actually deployed to ~/.cursor/rules/recommended-tools.mdc is never removed. Both global install paths (base scripts/lib/global-toolstack/install-body.sh:129-131 and install-recommended-tools-cursor.sh --global:72-75) copy scripts/lib/global-toolstack/global-recommended-tools.mdc, whose description is 'Global recommended tools — five_tool_routed stack (always enforced)'. RULES only knows the project variant 'SB recommended tools — full enforcement in Cursor'. The leftover is an alwaysApply rule. It keeps telling every Cursor workspace to enforce the SB five-tool stack via ~/.cursor/toolstack.json, which the same run moves away.
issues.evidence: HOME=home6 with base global-recommended-tools.mdc, agentmemory, leanctx and token-compression-enforcement rules -> 'kept: .../rules/recommended-tools.mdc: named like a Silver Bullet rule but the description differs'; the other 3 moved.
issues.suggested_fix: Accept both descriptions for recommended-tools (map name -> set of descriptions). Add a test seeded with the base global variant.

issues.problem: The whole ~/.cursor/hooks/toolstack directory is moved, including user files in it that Silver Bullet did not deploy, while their hooks.json entries are (correctly) kept. A user hook placed there is left pointing at a moved file.
issues.evidence: Seeded toolstack/mygate.sh with hooks.json entry 'bash <C>/hooks/toolstack/mygate.sh'. After the run, the entry is still in hooks.json and the file is under .silver-bullet-legacy-backup/.../hooks/toolstack/mygate.sh.
issues.suggested_fix: Move only the files the base install-body.sh deployed (TOOLSTACK_GATES + common.sh + the .py/verify/install files). Leave the directory when anything else remains, or at least report kept hook entries that point into a moved path.

issues.problem: Parent-directory symlinks are followed. If ~/.cursor/.silver-bullet, ~/.cursor/rules or ~/.cursor/plugins/cache/<mkt> is a symlink, matching files are moved out of the symlink target outside ~/.cursor. Only the leaf is symlink-checked.
issues.evidence: home2: .silver-bullet -> elsewhere/state, rules -> elsewhere/rules, cache/alo-labs-agent-plugins -> elsewhere/cache. The run moved elsewhere/state/site-session.json, elsewhere/rules/leanctx.mdc and elsewhere/cache/silver-bullet.
issues.suggested_fix: Skip (and report) when any path component under cursor_home is a symlink, e.g. compare path.resolve().parent with the lexical parent.

issues.problem: Per-step handling catches only ConfigError. An OSError in a move (or an unreadable common.sh) aborts the run with a traceback, after hooks.json has been rewritten and with the toolstack still in place.
issues.evidence: A regular file at ~/.cursor/.silver-bullet-legacy-backup gives rc=1 with a NotADirectoryError traceback; hooks.json was already rewritten and hooks/toolstack was not moved.
issues.suggested_fix: Catch OSError per step as well, report it and continue.

issues.problem: Not all sibling conflicts are keep-the-deletion. The modify/delete conflicts are all Cursor-only mirrors (keep the deletion). The content conflicts are of two kinds. Most are HC-deleted cursor code that the sibling rewrote (H4b merge-token-compression-config.py, its tests: drop the sibling side). The rest are line-level semantic merges: G1/G3 deploy-tier.sh and pre-release-host-isolation, G5 orchestrator-parent.sh (G5's rewrite replaces HC's regex edit), and H4a/H4b gate libs where HC changed the ~/.cursor fallbacks to ~/.claude. issues.evidence: git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD fix/<b> for each sibling.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the planned order (HC last among code packages, after H4a/H4b).
